title: Propagate message-level metadata and normalize logprob serialization for v1/chat.completions (framed tool-delta + heartbeat)
author: Avery Chen
commits: f81d3ea - add logprob serialization shim and tests for token-deltas
c9f4b2b - implement framed tool-delta envelope and heartbeat in stream coordinator
description:
Motivation: users relying on OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity have reported subtle incompatibilities when clients expect message-level metadata (role hints, message ids, provenance) to be preserved across streaming fragments and when logprobs are requested in combination with function/tool calls. This PR aims to (1) reliably propagate message-level metadata through the chat adapter and stream framing layers, (2) normalize logprob serialization so OpenAI-style token deltas and partial logprobs are stable across fragment boundaries, and (3) introduce a small framed "tool-delta" envelope and heartbeat frame to reduce client-side reconstruction complexity and improve tool/function call resilience.

Summary of changes: - Propagate message.metadata from the API adapter through chat session state and into stream frames. Message-level keys are namespaced under "rw_meta" when necessary to avoid collisions. This preserves role aliases and message ids for downstream consumers. - Replace ad-hoc logprob partials with a normalized OpenAI-compatible token-delta schema. The serializer emits a consistent token index and score map per fragment and includes a "continuation" flag to indicate that subsequent frames contain token-index increments. - Introduce a minimal framed envelope for tool/function outputs ("tool-delta") that separates tool stdout/stderr/structured JSON from the assistant text stream. This reduces accidental JSON merging and makes it trivial to rehydrate tool outputs on the client. - Add a lightweight heartbeat frame ("hb") emitted when the stream is idle for >250ms to help clients maintain connection health and avoid misinterpreting gaps as EOF. - Backcompat: adapter will accept both the old unframed tool output and the new framed-tool-delta; downstream consumers can opt into strict-mode via query param or header (x-rw-strict-chatv1). - Tests: unit tests for serializer edge cases, integration tests that assert metadata survive fragmentation and reconnection, and an e2e streaming test to validate heartbeat and tool-delta reassembly. - Docs: update OpenAPI examples and the chat compatibility guide with sample client rehydration code.

Checklist: - [x] preserve message-level metadata across all adapter layers - [x] stable logprob token-delta schema with continuation semantics - [x] framed tool-delta envelope implemented and backward-compatible - [x] heartbeat frame implemented and tested - [x] unit/integration/e2e tests added - [x] docs and console example updated

Compatibility notes: This change is backward-compatible by default. Clients that rely on the previous inline tool output behavior will continue to work. We provide a strict-mode header and a short migration guide for clients that want to require the framed-tool-delta envelope. The logprob schema is additive: older clients that ignore the new fields will still receive primary assistant text. Performance: added negligible overhead (small extra envelope bytes); verified no measurable latency regression in cpu-bound tests. Rollout plan: deploy to Canary, monitor e2e-streaming metrics and telemetry (stream fragmented error rate, tool reassembly failures) for 48 hours, then canary-to-main rollout.
review_thread: Jordan Patel: Can we avoid namespacing collisions by using a reserved prefix? Suggested 'rw_meta' to be explicit.
Avery Chen: Updated to 'rw_meta' across the adapter and added a short doc paragraph explaining the namespace. Tests added to assert no name collisions.
Samira Lopez: The heartbeat interval seems aggressive in high-throughput scenarios. Could we gate it behind a per-connection config?
Avery Chen: Heartbeat is configurable (default 250ms). For high-throughput connections it auto-suppresses when tokens/frames are emitted frequently. Added tests for suppression behavior.
Ethan Ruiz: Integration test flaked on rerun due to stream ordering; added a deterministic reorder buffer in test harness. Approving after green CI.
Jordan Patel: ✅ Looks good to me — merging after CI
release_notes: Stabilizes v1/chat.completions parity: preserves message-level metadata across stream fragments, standardizes logprob token-delta serialization, adds framed tool-delta envelope and idle heartbeat for improved streaming robustness. Backward-compatible by default; migration guide provided.
